subject: POC observability onboarding + success criteria (next steps)
message_1_subject: POC observability onboarding + success criteria (next steps)
message_1_body:
Hi Evan —

Great conversation earlier today. Quick recap and proposed plan so we’re aligned before the POC kicks off next week. Please confirm or flag edits.

High-level scope:
- Evaluate Redwood inference performance and observability during a 2-week POC using a production-like KindleAI workload (avg. seq len ~350 tokens, bursty 40–60 RPS).
- Focus areas: latency/SLO, error rates, model fallbacks, and cost per 1k tokens under batching/kv-cache.

Proposed success criteria (suggested, please prioritize):
1) 95th percentile generation latency <= 300ms for 512-token windows under steady-state load.
2) Request error rate < 0.5% (5xx & timeouts).
3) End-to-end tracing shows request path and token-level emit timings for >= 90% of requests.
4) Observability dashboards surface: per-model latency, per-route QPS, KV cache hit ratio, GPU utilization, and token cost estimate.
5) Exportable logs to your SIEM for audit (fields: request_id, model, route, latency_ms, user_tier).

Proposed evaluation plan & timeline:
- Day 0 (Wed 10/14): onboarding call — credentials, network setup, and attach Redwood agent for log export.
- Day 1–3: baseline runs (low load) to validate telemetry pipelines and dashboards.
- Day 4–10: scaled runs with production traffic replay.
- Day 11–14: readout and decision meeting (metrics + recordings).

Ownership (Redwood / KindleAI):
- Redwood: dashboard templates, tracing instrumentation, export connectors (LA/ELK/Splunk), test harness for load replay.
- KindleAI: sample datasets, expected SLO targets, security contact for SOC2 artifacts.

Attachments: poc-observability-checklist.xlsx (workback schedule), sample-dashboards.png (example dashboard set), redwood-dataflow-diagram.pdf (telemetry flow).

Next steps / asks for KindleAI:
- Confirm priority success criteria (which of the five are must-haves vs nice-to-have).
- Provide IP ranges for outbound connectivity and the persona/account to use for log forwarding.
- Share any compliance constraints that would affect log export retention or PII masking.

If that looks good I’ll lock the kickoff for 10/14 11:00am PT and loop in our infra engineer to start the VPC peering checklist.

Thanks —
Dylan
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
D: +1 415-555-0182

--
Attachments referenced above.
message_2_subject: Re: POC observability onboarding + success criteria (next steps)
message_2_body:
Thanks, Dylan — good recap. Priya and I reviewed and we’re aligned on scope with a couple of edits.

Priority success criteria (must-haves):
- #1 95th percentile latency <= 300ms (must)
- #2 Error rate < 0.5% (must)
- #4 Dashboards with per-route QPS, latency buckets, KV cache hit ratio (must)

Nice-to-have: token-cost estimates and full token-level timing traces for every request (we understand that may be sampled).

Security notes: looping in Ian Rogers (external security consultant) to validate log fields for SOC2 / retention policy. We cannot send raw user prompt text offsite; fields must be redacted or hashed before export. We can provide a masking spec by end of day 10/14.

Kickoff: 10/14 at 11:00am PT works for us. We’ll provide a small test corpus and IP ranges by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Evan
Director, Platform Engineering — KindleAI
